prerequisites: CONTINUUM MECHANICS: TENSOR FORMULATION OF STRESSES AND STRAINS, EQUILIBRIUM AND COMPATIBILITY, ISOTROPIC AND ORTHOTROPIC BEHAVIOUR, ELASTIC BEHAVIOUR AND HOOKE’S LAW.
MECHANICS OF MATERIALS: DUCTILE AND BRITTLE BEHAVIOUR, BASIC CONCEPTS OF STATIC STRENGTH.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the theoretical and practical knowledge required to use scientific instrumentation for measuring displacements and strains in structural materials.

Be able to analyse and interpret the results of experiments concerning the measurement of the stress–strain state of materials, components or structures, with the aim of characterising their mechanical behaviour under service conditions.
Cover a substantial part of the knowledge required for Level 2 personnel involved in non-destructive testing according to the EN ISO 9712 standard, specifically concerning strain-gauge measurements.

Learn the operating principles of different types of universal material testing machines and be able to implement the procedures of the main methods used for the mechanical characterisation of materials.
Apply, in the laboratory, the knowledge acquired regarding the characterisation of the mechanical behaviour of isotropic and orthotropic materials.
Understand and implement the recommendations typically provided by the main standards concerning the characterisation of the static and fatigue strength of materials.
Implement experimental set-ups and use them to perform measurements.
Select the specific analysis technique according to the type of material, component and information to be obtained.
Choose and adjust the instrumentation according to the type of measurement.
Prepare a report presenting the results, including their interpretation and the limits of applicability of the method.

Perform strain and displacement measurements useful for the mechanical characterisation of materials and to design experimental measurements aimed at assessing the structural integrity of a component or structure.

Critically select the experimental set-up most suitable for the characterisation of a given mechanical behaviour, according to the type of material, in order to obtain the main stiffness and strength data required for structural design.
Play an active role in data collection, data analysis and in the formulation of a critical summary judgement regarding the experimental activities carried out.
Evaluate problems related to the mechanical characterisation of materials and to interpret the prescriptions and recommendations typically found in international standards.

Develop skills related to the presentation of measurement results, the description and presentation of the characteristics of the implemented experimental set-ups, and the processing of results according to specific codes, standards or theoretical procedures.
Describe, using appropriate terminology and technical awareness, the characteristics of the measurement set-ups used in experimental mechanics.

syllabus_topics: Review of stress and strain tensors and fundamentals of elasticity theory.
Hooke’s law and its generalisation to anisotropic materials.
General overview of the strength of structural materials: brittle and ductile behaviour, static and fatigue failure, fatigue crack propagation.
General framework of tests for the mechanical characterisation of materials.
Standards for the mechanical characterisation of materials.
Overview of the exponential hardening law and the Ramberg–Osgood law.
Tensile and compressive characterisation of isotropic and orthotropic materials – theory.
Flexural and shear characterisation of isotropic and orthotropic materials – theory.
Fatigue characterisation – theory.
Characterisation of materials with respect to fatigue crack propagation resistance – theory.
Strain-gauge measurements: characteristics of strain gauges.
Strain-gauge measurements: criteria for selecting strain gauges.
Strain-gauge measurements: resistance measurement circuit.
Strain-gauge measurements: measurement of simple stress states.
Strain-gauge measurements: influence of cables.
Strain-gauge measurements: bridge calibration.
Strain-gauge measurements: measurement and analysis of strains in plane fields.
Strain-gauge measurements: strain analysis in anisotropic materials.
Optical methods: Digital Image Correlation methods.
Principle of the 2D-DIC method.
Displacements and strains in continuum mechanics.
Subset deformation and shape functions.
Determination of the strain field.
Correlation functions and calculation methods.
Strain calculation.
Experimental implementation: specimen preparation and speckle characteristics.
Image acquisition.
Systematic and random errors in DIC methods.
Description of universal material testing machines and main accessories for mechanical measurements.
Implementation of tensile tests on isotropic and orthotropic materials using servo-hydraulic and electromechanical testing machines.
Implementation of compression tests on isotropic and orthotropic materials using servo-hydraulic and electromechanical testing machines.
Implementation of stress corrosion cracking tests using an electromechanical testing machine.
Implementation of flexural and shear tests on isotropic and orthotropic materials using servo-hydraulic and electromechanical testing machines.
Implementation of fatigue tests on isotropic and orthotropic materials using a servo-hydraulic testing machine.
Implementation of crack propagation tests on metallic materials.
Crack gauges, COD gauge and back-face strain measurements using a servo-hydraulic testing machine.
Strain-gauge measurements 1: installation and inspection of a single-grid strain gauge on a steel beam.
Strain-gauge measurements 2: measurement of strain-gauge signals using different configurations.
Strain-gauge measurements 3: influence of cables on strain-gauge measurements.
Strain-gauge measurements 4: measurements using strain-gauge rosettes.
Strain-gauge measurements 5: measurements using strain-gauge load cells and data loggers.
DIC 1: implementation of a 2D-DIC set-up using the NCORR software.
Signal acquisition.
Preparation of the test report.
teaching_methods: Strain-gauge activities (installation and measurement in equipped classroom)
Material testing in Machine Design laboratory (Department of Industrial Engineering)

assessment_methods.method: Discussion of a written report concerning course exercises and laboratory activities

assessment_rules: Learning outcomes will be assessed through an oral examination based on the discussion of a written report concerning the course exercises and laboratory activities. The report, prepared by a group of 2-4 students, will include exercises on material test data and contributes to the final grade. Students must send their PDF report to the instructor one day before the exam. The examination consists of a theoretical question and a review of the laboratory report, assessing comparison of techniques, clarity, use of graphics, and report quality.
